note: Sat 21 Nov 2026 run, as of the Fri 20 Nov US close (latest completed session; weekend, markets closed). Friday was a sharp, distinct escalation: S&P -3.70% to 6910.39 (5th straight down day), VIX +26.2% to 35.89 (highest since March), driven by Reuters' Nvidia SEC-accounting-probe report (-14%, ~$500bn erased) and Google's reported ~20% Broadcom-TPU-order cut (AVGO -11.4%, MRVL -10%), landing on monthly options expiration (~55-57% of SPY/QQQ negative gamma rolling off). Gold/silver/miners fell in lockstep with equities (GLD -3.67%, SLV -6.74%, GDX -5.00%) despite softer US data, read as margin-call-driven liquidation rather than a fresh metals catalyst. CNN Fear & Greed fell to 14 (Extreme Fear, from 19 Thursday) -- lowest since 30 Mar 2026. Breadth and weekly fund-flow data for this run carry wider-than-usual source disagreement (flagged explicitly below) since several Friday-close figures are still settling across providers as of Saturday morning SGT.

fearGreed.note: CNN's own API (production.dataviz.cnn.io, cnn.com/markets/fear-and-greed) again returned 418/451 to automated fetches; value 14 is corroborated across 4+ independent citations of CNN's own number (TokenPost, CryptoBriefing, KuCoin, CryptoNews.net), lowest since 30 Mar 2026, down 26 points in 8 sessions. ONE conflicting third-party mirror (fgscore.com) showed a headline score of 10, not reconciled -- flagged rather than silently resolved. Crypto value is ambiguous between 10-12 depending on alternative.me's daily UTC rollover timing; 11 used as the midpoint. Component readings are directionally sourced from fgscore.com's table (which carries the 10-vs-14 discrepancy noted above) cross-checked against fragmentary Nov 18-20 citations -- treat as approximate, not CNN's exact feed.

BofA/EPFR: global equity funds +$66.6bn, US equities +$45.6bn (7th straight week), tech funds +$5.4bn (8th straight week), EM equities +$8.3bn (8th straight week); bonds -$7.4bn (first outflow since April 2025) and EM debt -$7.5bn (most since April 2020); crypto funds -$1.1bn; BofA's own Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.1 from 7.4. Lipper: US equity funds +$45.71bn (largest since 23 Sep, 3rd straight week), tech funds +$10.3bn (largest since 16 Jun), global equity funds +$59.23bn (9th straight week); US bond funds -$5.58bn (first outflow in 4 weeks, high-yield -$2.31bn, long Treasury -$2.64bn); money market -$19.12bn (2nd straight weekly outflow).
